deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page belongs to Gauss's early work on the lemniscatic functions (c. 1797–98). sl φ is written as a quotient M/N of entire functions. The series implied by the page are M(φ) = φ − φ^5/60 + …, which is Gauss's P(φ) = φ − 2φ^5/5! + 36φ^9/9! − …, and N(φ) = 1 + φ^4/12 − φ^8/10080 + …, which is Q(φ) = 1 + 2φ^4/4! − 4φ^8/8! + …. Likewise cl φ = μ/ν. The next page continues with N^4, N(…) series and the numerical value e^{π/2} = 4.81048, i.e. the same research programme.

(1) Top lines: series comparison. Gauss writes M²+N² with φ suppressed (φ = 1):
- M²+N² = 1 + φ² + φ⁴/6 − φ⁶/30 + 17φ⁸/2520 + …
- Check: N² contributes 1 + φ⁴/6 + (1/144 − 1/5040)φ⁸ = … + 17φ⁸/2520. M² contributes φ² − φ⁶/30.
- He sets beside it ν² = 1 + φ²/2 − φ⁴/24 + φ⁶/240 + 17φ⁸/40320 + ….
- The comparison evidently tests whether ν² equals M²+N². It does not. The crossed-out √(4M²N²μ²ν² + (M⁴+N⁴)²) = √(M2² + N2²) below is the abandoned attempt to define ν2 that way.
- [My observation, not on the page:] with w = (1+i)φ/2, the given ν² series coincides through φ⁸ with N(w)² − i·M(w)². This fits the note "μν = N(1+√−1)", i.e. the use of complex multiplication by 1+i.

(2) Duplication. N2 = M⁴+N⁴ and M2 = 2MNμν, so that
- sl 2φ = M2/N2 = 2MNμν/(M⁴+N⁴).
- Equivalently sl 2φ = 2 s c (1+s²)/(1+s⁴), with s = sl φ and c = cl φ.
- The two forms agree only with a normalisation in which ν² is proportional to M²+N², tied to μ²/ν² = (N²−M²)/(N²+M²).

(3) Basic relation, written μμ = ((NN−MM)/(NN+MM))·νν. This is cl²φ = (1 − sl²φ)/(1 + sl²φ).

(4) Duplication of cl. Gauss computes μ2/ν2 = (c² − s²)/(2 − c² − s²), using c² = μμ/νν and s² = MM/NN. Substituting (3) gives
- (N⁴ − 2M²N² − M⁴)/(N⁴ + 2M²N² − M⁴), i.e. cl 2φ = (1 − 2s² − s⁴)/(1 + 2s² − s⁴).
- The cleared form (NNμμ − MMνν)/(2ννNN − …) is left unfinished. Its denominator should read 2ννNN − NNμμ − MMνν.

(5) A second, different expression is also recorded: (μμNN − ννMM)/(NNνν − MMμμ), and its square root, both labelled μ2/ν2. This equals (c² − s²)/(1 − s²c²). The addition theorem gives cl 2φ = (c² − s²)/(1 + s²c²), so the sign is wrong.

(6) Bottom: the Pythagorean-type relation of the lemniscate.
- Correct form: s² + c² + s²c² = 1. Gauss first writes the last term as M⁴μ⁴/(N⁴ν⁴) and clears denominators to M⁴μ⁴ + μ²ν²N⁴ + M²N²ν⁴ = N⁴ν⁴ (inherits the slip).
- He ends with the correct factorised form (1 + MM/NN)(1 + μμ/νν) = 2.
- The line μ2ν2 = M⁴N⁴ + μ⁴ν⁴ is a tentative, unverified guess for the product of the duplicated functions.
errors: In 1 = MM/NN + μμ/νν + M⁴μ⁴/(N⁴ν⁴) the last term should be M²μ²/(N²ν²), since sl²+cl²+sl²cl² = 1. The cleared equation M⁴μ⁴ + μμννN⁴ + MMNNν⁴ = N⁴ν⁴ inherits this slip; the correct form is M²ν² + μ²N² + M²μ² = N²ν². The final line (1+MM/NN)(1+μμ/νν) = 2 is correct.

μ2/ν2 = (μμNN − ννMM)/(NNνν − MMμμ) equals (c² − s²)/(1 − s²c²). The correct cl 2φ is (c² − s²)/(1 + s²c²), so the sign in the denominator is wrong. The adjacent square root of this expression is likewise not cl 2φ.
The denominator written 'M⁴+2MMNN−M⁴' must be N⁴ + 2M²N² − M⁴.
The cleared fraction (NNμμ − MMνν)/(2ννNN − …) is unfinished; the denominator should be 2ννNN − NNμμ − MMνν.
The top two series show ν² ≠ M²+N², so any step that silently assumes ν² = M²+N² (e.g. the crossed-out √(M2²+N2²)) is invalid; Gauss crossed it out.
μ2ν2 = M⁴N⁴ + μ⁴ν⁴ is not justified on the page; it remains an unverified guess.

results.what: sl φ = M/N with M = φ − φ⁵/60 + …, N = 1 + φ⁴/12 − …; series of M²+N² up to φ⁸
results.modern_name: Representation of the lemniscatic sine as a quotient of entire functions (theta-function quotient)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (unpublished, 1797–98; Werke III/X), later Abel and Jacobi via theta functions

results.what: Duplication sl 2φ = 2MNμν/(M⁴+N⁴) and cl 2φ = (1 − 2s² − s⁴)/(1 + 2s² − s⁴)
results.modern_name: Duplication formulas for the lemniscatic functions
results.usually_credited_to: Fagnano (1718) / Euler; in this form Gauss

results.what: cl² = (1 − sl²)/(1 + sl²), equivalently (1 + sl²)(1 + cl²) = 2
results.modern_name: Fundamental algebraic relation between sl and cl

results.what: Expression of ν² through M, N at (1+i)φ/2 (my inference from the series)
results.modern_name: Complex multiplication of the lemniscatic functions by 1+i

deep.surprise_reason: Working notes on the lemniscatic sine as M/N, its duplication and the sl–cl relation are part of Gauss's well-documented 1797–98 lemniscate research (Werke III, X, diary). Nothing here goes beyond what is known to be his.
